newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hargraves plans to boost gold output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hargraves plans to boost gold output.

text.p: Hargraves Resources NL said on Wednesday it planned to boost gold production at its Brown's Creek gold mine in central New South Wales to 70,000 ounces a year by installing a new grinding mill.
The mine produced 44,000 ounces in the year to June 1996.
Managing director Peter Prentice said the plant upgrade would cost less than A$2.5 million and was expected to be commissioned by April 1997.
The mine also produced 1,000 tonnes of copper metal in concentrates in 1995/96, its first full year of operation.
Hargraves said the expansion was based on excellent results achieved from deep exploration drilling in the past six months.
The drilling showed that not only did the ore body continue at depth but it was considerably thicker and contained higher grades of gold and copper than the current run of the mine.

"The success of the exploration at Brown's Creek and on tenements surrounding the mine has prompted the company to initiate a major exploration thrust, spending up to A$12 million over the next 12 months, targeting the Brown's Creek mine and a number of advanced targets within Hargrave's exploration areas," Prentice said in a statement.
Prentice said the exploration programmes would be funded by a recent A$5.4 million share placement combined with cash flows from the Brown's Creek mine.
The total resource at Brown's Creek was 1.36 million tonnes grading 6.1 grams per tonne gold and 0.44 percent copper as of June 30, Prentice said.
